**Step 1 – Parse the policy**

Policy: *“A plan or recommendation made for the user holds only while the personal circumstances it was based on still hold.”*

This means the memory can be valid **only if** the factual condition that justified it is still true for the user.  
Thus we need to find every **fact** that describes a circumstance, and pair it with the memory whose text explicitly says that circumstance is the reason for the plan.

The policy contains **no “or”** wording, so there is a **single group** that must satisfy **all** of its conditions (i.e., the condition derived from the policy).

**Step 2 – Identify conditions**

The condition for each memory is: *“The factual statement (the ‘circumstance’) that appears in the memory’s justification must currently hold true for the user.”*  
For each memory we look for the exact fact that directly supplies that justification.

**Step 3 – Match facts to memories**

| Memory (id)                              | Reason given in memory text                              | Matching fact (id)                              |
|------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| **m_003a6d** – woodworking passion      | “woodworking is the user’s main passion …”                | e_0029b8 – “Woodworking is my main passion …” |
| **m_009abe** – four weekly strength workouts | “user has been keeping to a routine of four strength training sessions each week” | e_005aa6 – “I’ve been keeping to a routine of four strength training sessions each week …” |
| **m_003475** – undergraduate schedule   | “user is currently an undergraduate …”                   | e_00e073 – “I’m currently an undergraduate …” |
| **m_00b168** – home‑buying focus        | “user has been zeroing in on buying a permanent home …”   | e_0004ed – “I’ve really been zeroing in on buying a permanent home …” |
| **m_00c1b9** – landscaping recovery need | “user knows they need 48 h after heavy landscaping”       | e_0005d8 – “I know my body well enough now to say that after a heavy day of landscaping, I need a full forty-eight hours …” |
| **m_0033e6** – coffee & cigarettes habit | “user’s energy doesn’t hold up unless they’re regularly having coffee and cigarettes” | e_00c673 – “I’ve noticed that my energy levels just don’t hold up unless I’m regularly having coffee and cigarettes.” |
| **m_00cce7** – blender‑review preference | “user ignores five‑star ratings and relies entirely on critical reviews” | e_004270 – “Even if a blender has thousands of five‑star ratings, I focus entirely …” |

All other facts (e_0041a1, e_0041a1‑duplicate, etc.) are either unrelated or serve as general background but are **not** the specific justification for any listed memory.

**Step 4 – Assemble the JSON**

The policy yields **one group** whose **all‑of** list contains each of the six condition‑item pairs above.

```json
{
  "groups": [
    {
      "all_of": [
        { "condition": "Woodworking is the user's main passion", "item": "e_0029b8" },
        { "condition": "User keeps four weekly strength‑training sessions", "item": "e_005aa6" },
        { "condition": "User is an undergraduate with an academic schedule", "item": "e_00e073" },
        { "condition": "User is focusing on buying a permanent home", "item": "e_0004ed" },
        { "condition": "User needs 48 h recovery after heavy landscaping", "item": "e_0005d8" },
        { "condition": "User’s energy only sustains coffee & cigarettes", "item": "e_00c673" },
        { "condition": "User prefers critical reviews over five‑star ratings for blenders", "item": "e_004270" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

This JSON exactly satisfies the policy: the memory is valid **only while** each listed condition (backed by its corresponding fact) continues to hold for the user.
